headline: Ideas emerge from combining existing elements in new ways—creativity is connection, not creation from nothing
universal_truth: Nothing comes from nothing; new things are always recombinations of old things
fun_facts: The printing press combined wine presses, movable type, and ink—all existing technologies
Studies show creative people consume more diverse content, giving them more elements to combine
Many inventions happen when ideas from one field are applied to solve problems in another
discussion_questions: Where do your best ideas come from?
How does exposure to diverse experiences affect creativity?
What unrelated ideas might you combine?

hook.script: Gutenberg combined wine presses with movable type. Darwin combined geology with biology. Steve Jobs combined calligraphy with computers. New ideas don't appear from nothing—they're born when existing ideas collide in new ways.

cliff.script: We imagine creativity as lightning bolts—sudden inspiration from nowhere. But if ideas come from combinations, what does that mean for becoming more creative?
cliff.prompt: How can you become more creative?

options.text: By exposing yourself to diverse ideas and experiences—more ingredients mean more possible combinations
options.response: Yes. Creative people read widely, explore different fields, and collect diverse experiences. They have more ingredients to combine. Creativity is a numbers game of connections.

options.text: By waiting for inspiration to strike
options.response: Inspiration happens, but you can increase its likelihood by filling your mind with raw material...

fact1.title: Adjacent Possible
fact1.script: Ideas can only combine with nearby ideas—what's called the 'adjacent possible.' You can't invent the internet in 1800; the building blocks weren't available. Creativity works with what exists, pushing into what just became possible.

fact2.title: Cross-Pollination
fact2.script: Many breakthroughs come from applying ideas from one field to another. Velcro came from burrs in fur. Resistance training uses physics in biology. The most creative people are often polymaths who connect distant fields.

fact3.title: Quantity Before Quality
fact3.script: Creative geniuses produce more—not just better. Edison had 1,093 patents. Picasso created 50,000 works. More attempts mean more combinations, and more combinations mean more chances for a great one.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Nothing comes from nothing. Ideas teach that new things are recombinations of old things. Fill your mind with diverse ingredients and let them collide.

outro.script: That's Day 182—welcome to July's Adventure month! Tomorrow, we'll explore how to think about thinking. Until then, seek ideas from outside your usual sources.

growTrack.title: Idea Collection - Gather Ingredients
growTrack.activity: Read, watch, or listen to something completely outside your usual interests today. A random Wikipedia article, a documentary on an unfamiliar topic, a magazine from a different field. Collect ingredients—creativity needs diverse raw material.
